text:
Priya Menon [14:02]: I have been through the draft supplier agreement, and clause 12 worries me.
Callum Rhodes [14:04]: Which part? [1]
Priya Menon [14:05]: The provision that lets the supplier raise prices at any time without notice. [2] , we would have no way of budgeting beyond the next quarter.
Callum Rhodes [14:07]: Agreed. I will propose that any increase be [3] to ninety days' written notice and capped at five percent a year.
Priya Menon [14:08]: That would be acceptable. [4] they refuse, we should escalate to the director.

choices: I recall that we negotiated the pricing mechanism at length, and the supplier accepted most of our proposals.
I recall that we negotiated the delivery schedule at length, and the supplier refused most of our proposals.
I recall that the supplier negotiated the pricing mechanism at length, and we accepted most of its proposals.
I recalled that we had negotiated the pricing mechanism at length, and the supplier would accept our proposals.
questions.explanation: Priya's reply is about a price clause, so the previous message must refer to the pricing mechanism; only the first does coherently.
'Otherwise' states the consequence if the clause stays: no way of budgeting.
'Subject to ninety days' written notice' is the fixed expression.
'Should they refuse' is an inverted conditional meaning 'if they refuse'.

text: Dear Mr. Lindqvist, this is a reminder from Harlow Dental Practice that your appointment is scheduled for Tuesday 9 June at 10.15 a.m. [1] Please arrive five minutes early so that the receptionist can update your records. If you are unable to attend, we should be [2] if you would call us at least twenty-four hours in advance, [3] a fee of £30 will be charged. You may [4] your appointment online using the link below. Thank you.

choices: Your hygienist this time will be Ms. Carvalho, who has taken over your care from Mr. Dunmore.
Your hygienist this time will be Ms. Carvalho, who has taken over the care of Mr. Dunmore.
Your appointment this time was with Ms. Carvalho, who took over your care from Mr. Dunmore.
Your hygienist this time will be Mr. Dunmore, who has taken over your care from Ms. Carvalho.
questions.explanation: The next sentence tells the patient to arrive early to update records, consistent with a change of practitioner; only the first is coherent.
'We should be grateful if you would call' is the polite formula; 'gracious' and 'graceful' describe manner and movement.
'Otherwise a fee of £30 will be charged' states the consequence of not calling in advance.
A patient may 'confirm' or 'cancel' an appointment online; 'confirm' means verify it; the others do not fit.
